Laboratory Rules Anyone working in the chemistry laboratory should follow certain rules and etiquettes. These rules, attention and etiquettes enable the students to
Practical Chemistry achieve more accurate results as well as to prevent any possible hazards.
Furthermore, the students will be accustomed with good working habits.
Followings are the rules to be followed by the students in chemistry laboratory.
1. Work patiently, diligently, wisely and carefully under the laboratory
rules. One should know how to set the experiment and note down the observation.
Start an experiment only after it is clear. Consult the teacher and note the important points.
Keep your working table always neat and clean. It is your duty to clean the working table after the experiment is finished.
Do not perform the unauthorized experiments and do not handle the unknown chemicals.
Handle the apparatus and chemicals with care. Do not touch the chemicals with hands.
Never come with vacant mind in the laboratory class. Come prepared for the concerned experiment. Bring the practical book, practical note book and a rough copy in the practical class.
Do not taste any chemicals in the laboratory. Do not smell unauthorized chemicals or gases. Smell the gases, if required, cautiously.
If an accident happens or a breakage occurs, report it immediately to the laboratory in-charge.
Care should be taken while heating sömething. Do not let the gas tap and water tap open while not in use.
Keep the reagent bottles of bench chemicals (which generally consist of dilute mineral acids, dil. NaOH and dil. NH40H) and rack chemicals at proper conditions at their proper places after their use.
Never bring the reagent bottles on you table.
Use the concentrated acids and bases carefully with the help of a glass tube.
Always put on aprons before starting the experiment.
Clean the apparatus before and after every use.
Do not make noise in the laboratory. Do not move in the laboratory unnecessarily.
Do not contaminate a chemical with another.
General Introduction Throw the breakages and waste substances int.qJ/ {he dust bins.
Take the apparatus from the store from the authorized person and submit them to the same place after finishing experiment.
Be punctual and regular in laboratory classes. Have the experiments in the practical note book signed regularly.
Start you experimental work with minimum amount of substance.
Do not use excess of the chemical substance unless otherwise stated.
Do not be careless in your work. Do each experiment carefully and independently. Handle each apparatus yourself.

Keep the mouth of the test tube away from you and your friends while heating conc. acids or performing any unknown reactions. Do not bring inflammable substances (e.g. ether, alcohol) near the Bunsen flame.
In case any leakage of the L.P. gas is noticed, inform the teachers or laboratory staff immediately.
Never take anything with you from the laboratory.
